1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115

118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |

165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |

This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

---

## 7. Integrated flowchart — screens × requirements × backend

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph T0["Screen 0 — Splash"]
        direction TB
        E01["GET /auth/session"]
    end

    subgraph T01["Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault · RF03"]
        direction TB
        E02b["Face ID / Touch ID / PIN — validated on the device, no backend call"]
        E02["POST /auth/login (if the session has fully expired)"]
    end

    subgraph T1["Screen 1 — Home (chat) · RF04, RF08, RF10"]
        direction TB
        E04["POST /chat/sessions"]
        E05["GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06["POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06b["POST .../messages/:userMessageId/retry"]
        E07["POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight"]
        E07b["POST /entries (save message)"]
    end

    subgraph T2["Screen 2 — Insertion modal · RF01, RF02"]
        direction TB
        E08["POST /media/ocr"]
        E09["POST /entries"]
    end

    subgraph T3["Screen 3 — Side menu"]
        direction TB
        E10["GET /chat/sessions"]
        E10b["'Novo Chat' button — opens T1 empty, backed by E04"]
    end

    subgraph T4["Screen 4 — My records · RF05, RF06, RF07"]
        direction TB
        E11["GET /entries (source/dateFrom/dateTo — no category)"]
        E12["GET /entries/search"]
        E15["POST /export/summary"]

        E16["GET /export/:jobId/download"]
    end

    subgraph T5["Screen 5 — Action plans (extension)"]
        direction TB

    end

    subgraph T6["Screen 6 — Settings · RF09, RNF05"]
        direction TB

    end

    T0 --> T01 --> T1
    T1 --> T2
    T1 --> T3
    T3 -->|Novo Chat| T1
    T3 --> T4
    T3 --> T5
    T3 --> T6

    style T5 fill:#FAEEDA,stroke:#BA7517,color:#412402
```

*(The amber "Action plans" subgraph marks the only screen with no backend calls — a product extension.)*

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

183	## 4. Special states that need extra care
184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |

1	# Feature Specification: P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `006-semantic-search-filter` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-17
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries: Let the user find entries by meaning and narrow them with filters, on the My Records screen, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF06) and its acceptance criteria; parameter in section 10. Prototype states: the search bar of 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros', 'Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro', and 'Tela 4 — Filtros ativos' (prototype extract, section 2.4, including the note that the backend has no category filter). Backend: GET /entries/search, GET /entries. Test material: docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md. Depends on RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-17
14	
15	- Q: The filter sheet's "TIPO DE ENTRADA" chips allow selecting more than one entry type at once, but both `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only a single `source` value per request, and every entry has exactly one `source` — so an entry can never match "every" selected type simultaneously. How should multiple selected entry-type chips be combined, and how should the request(s) be built? → A: Entries having ANY of the selected types are included (OR among the entry-type chips themselves), while that combined set is still ANDed with the active date range and search term. To build it, the app fires one request per selected entry type (each carrying the same `q`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), merges the responses, de-duplicates by entry ID, and re-sorts the combined set (by relevance when a search term is active, otherwise reverse-chronological, matching RF07) before rendering — preserving the prototype's multi-select affordance without requiring a backend change. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: When the user is scrolled through a search result list (an active `q`) and nears the bottom, should the app try to load a further page, given `GET /entries/search` has no `cursor` parameter and caps results at `limit` (max 50)? → A: No — while a search term is active, the single fetch (up to `limit`) is the complete result set for that query; "scrollable" means scrolling within what is already loaded, not triggering a further fetch. Clearing the search text returns to `GET /entries`'s existing cursor-based infinite scroll (RF07) for filter-only or unfiltered browsing. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: With a 300 ms debounce and no server-side throttle on `GET /entries/search` (per its own API summary), could a slow, older response arrive after a newer request's response and overwrite it with stale results? → A: Yes, so the app MUST treat only the most recently fired request (per debounce fire, filter change, chip removal, or "Limpar filtros") as authoritative — discarding the response of any earlier, now-superseded request for the same screen state, never applying a late-arriving stale response over a newer one. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Finding an entry by what it means, not what it says (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user wants to find something they wrote about even though they can't remember the exact words they used. They type a term into the search bar on "Meus Registros" and get back entries that are about that topic, including ones that never use the literal word they typed.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF06 and the capability that sets this screen apart from a plain keyword filter — without it, the feature delivers no value beyond what RF07's list already provides.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding the three entries from `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md` (none of which contains the literal search term) and confirming each documented search term (`ansiedade`, `cansaço`, `gratidão`) returns its matching entry.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the seeded entry that describes racing thoughts and a tight chest the night before a presentation (no occurrence of the word "ansiedade"), **When** the user searches "ansiedade", **Then** that entry appears in the results.
32	2. **Given** the user is typing a search term, **When** they type several characters in quick succession, **Then** exactly one search request is sent, 300 ms after they stop typing — not one request per keystroke.
33	3. **Given** the user clears the search text completely, **When** the field becomes empty, **Then** the screen returns to showing results based only on whatever filters are still active (or the full list, if none are active), without sending a search for an empty term.
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Narrowing the list with filters (Priority: P1)
38	
39	A user wants to see only entries from a particular date range and/or a particular capture method (text, audio, photo, chat), without necessarily typing any search term. They open the filter sheet, choose criteria, apply them, and see a narrowed list.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: Equally core to RF06 as semantic search — the requirement explicitly treats "semantic similarity combined with metadata filters" as a single capability, and filtering alone (with no search text) must work correctly on its own.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the filter sheet on an account with entries of mixed dates and sources, applying a date range and an entry-type selection together, and confirming the result list contains only entries that satisfy both.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the filter sheet is open, **When** the user picks a date-range option (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês) and one or more entry-type chips (manual, áudio, foto, chat) and taps "Aplicar", **Then** the list narrows to entries that fall within the chosen date range AND have one of the chosen entry types — the date range and the entry-type selection are ANDed with each other, while multiple selected entry types are ORed among themselves (an entry has exactly one type, so it can never match more than one at a time).
48	2. **Given** the filter sheet's "CATEGORIA" chip group (trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), **When** the user taps one of those chips and applies the sheet, **Then** the result list is unaffected by that selection, because the backend has no category filter — the chips exist for visual fidelity to the prototype only.
49	3. **Given** the filter sheet is open, **When** the user taps "Limpar" inside the sheet, **Then** every selection in the sheet resets before it is applied.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - Seeing and clearing what's currently applied (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A user who has applied one or more filters, with or without a search term, wants to glance at the screen and immediately understand what is currently narrowing their results, and be able to remove any single criterion or all of them at once.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: A usability layer on top of Stories 1 and 2 — the underlying narrowing already works without it, but the requirement's own acceptance criteria call out that filters must be clearable without restarting the screen, and the prototype dedicates a distinct state to this.
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by applying two filters, confirming a chip appears for each with the funnel button shown filled, removing one chip and confirming only that criterion drops out, then using "Limpar filtros" and confirming the screen returns to its unfiltered list without reloading.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** one or more filters are applied, **When** the screen re-renders, **Then** a removable chip appears under the search bar for each active filter, a "Limpar filtros" link is shown, and the funnel button displays its filled/active state.
64	2. **Given** active-filter chips are showing, **When** the user taps the removable control on a single chip, **Then** only that criterion is removed and the result list updates to reflect the remaining active criteria (or the full list, if none remain) — the screen is not reloaded or reset.
65	3. **Given** active-filter chips are showing, **When** the user taps "Limpar filtros", **Then** every applied filter and any active search text is cleared and the screen returns to the same full, unfiltered list RF07 already shows, without navigating away from or restarting the screen.
66	
67	---
68	
69	### User Story 4 - Cached results stay trustworthy through a connectivity blip (Priority: P3)
70	
71	A user is viewing search or filter results when the connection drops and later comes back. What they see while offline comes from the local cache, and once reconnected, the list reconciles with the server without showing the same entry twice or leaving stale results behind unnoticed.
72	
73	**Why this priority**: A correctness property layered on top of Stories 1–3 rather than a feature of its own; it depends on search and filtering already producing a result list to keep consistent, and it protects against a subtle trust-eroding bug rather than blocking the core flow.
74	
75	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a search/filter result list, simulating a loss and restoration of connectivity, and confirming the list shown offline matches the cache, with no duplicated entries once the server is reachable again.
76	
77	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
78	
79	1. **Given** a search or filter result list is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the previously loaded results remain visible and scrollable from the local cache.
80	2. **Given** results were shown from cache while offline, **When** the connection is restored, **Then** the list reconciles with what the server currently returns for the same search/filter criteria, with every entry appearing exactly once (no duplicates).
81	
82	---
83	
84	### Edge Cases
85	
86	- A search and/or filter combination matches zero entries on an account that does have entries: the screen shows a distinct "no results for this search/filter" message, not RF07's account-wide "Nenhum registro ainda" empty state, and offers a way to adjust or clear the applied criteria from there.
87	- The user types a term, then deletes it entirely before the 300 ms debounce fires: no request is ever sent for the abandoned partial text.
88	- A search request or a filtered fetch fails outright (timeout, malformed response, or the device is offline when the request would be sent): the screen shows a clear, retryable error without discarding whatever cached results are already displayed, and without attempting any write.
89	- The session expires while a search or a filtered view is active: the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay (RF07) handles it, and once resolved, the active search text and filters are still applied — they are not silently cleared by the session event.
90	- A filter is applied together with an active search term at the same time (not shown explicitly acting together anywhere in the prototype): both narrow the same result set together under AND logic, consistent with the requirement's general rule that "two or more filters applied at the same time narrow results with AND logic."
91	- A new search, filter change, or clear action fires while an earlier request for the same screen is still in flight: only the most recently fired request's response is ever applied to the screen; any earlier, now-superseded response is discarded so a slow stale response can never overwrite newer results.
92	- An active search term's result list already shows every entry the backend returned for that query (up to its `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of that list does not trigger a further fetch, since `GET /entries/search` has no pagination cursor; only clearing the search term resumes RF07's existing cursor-based infinite scroll for filter-only or unfiltered browsing.
93	
94	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
95	
96	### Functional Requirements
97	
98	- **FR-001**: The system MUST wire the search bar already present on "Meus Registros" to `GET /entries/search`'s `q` parameter, returning entries ranked by semantic similarity to the typed term rather than by exact keyword matching.
99	- **FR-002**: Text entered in the search bar MUST be debounced at the fixed 300 ms parameter (requirements section 10), so that a burst of fast typing results in exactly one search request fired after the user pauses, never one request per keystroke; clearing the search text to empty MUST NOT itself trigger a search-for-nothing request.
100	- **FR-003**: The system MUST provide a filter sheet, reachable via the existing funnel button, offering a single-choice date-range selector (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, mapped to `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) and a multi-select entry-type selector (manual, áudio, foto, chat, mapped to `source`), with "Aplicar" committing the current selections and "Limpar" resetting the sheet's own selections before they are applied. Because `source` accepts only a single value per request, selecting more than one entry-type chip MUST be implemented as one request per selected type, with the responses merged, de-duplicated by entry ID, and re-sorted before being rendered (see Clarifications).
101	- **FR-004**: The filter sheet's "CATEGORIA" chip group (trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações) MUST be rendered for visual fidelity to the prototype but MUST NOT filter the result list or send any category-related parameter to the backend, since neither `GET /entries` nor `GET /entries/search` implements a category or tag filter.
102	- **FR-005**: Any combination of currently active criteria — date range, the set of selected entry types, and an active search term — MUST narrow the result list using AND logic across those three axes at once, never OR logic between them. Within the entry-type axis itself, selecting more than one type MUST include an entry if it matches ANY of the selected types (OR among types), since each entry has exactly one `source` value and could otherwise never satisfy more than one type at a time.
103	- **FR-005a**: A new search, filter change, or clear action MUST be treated as superseding any still-in-flight earlier request for the same screen: the response of an earlier, now-superseded request MUST be discarded rather than applied, so a slower stale response can never overwrite the results of a more recent request.
104	- **FR-005b**: While an active search term (`q`) is in effect, the result list MUST consist of the single bounded response already returned by `GET /entries/search` (up to its `limit`); scrolling within that list MUST NOT trigger a further fetch. Clearing the search term MUST resume `GET /entries`'s existing cursor-based infinite scroll (RF07) for filter-only or unfiltered browsing.
105	- **FR-006**: Whenever one or more filters are applied, the screen MUST show a removable chip for each active filter under the search bar, a "Limpar filtros" link, and the funnel button in its filled/active visual state.
106	- **FR-007**: Removing a single active-filter chip MUST drop only that criterion and refresh the result list accordingly; activating "Limpar filtros" MUST drop every active filter and any active search text at once; neither action MUST reload or restart the screen.
107	- **FR-008**: Clearing every active filter and search term MUST return the screen to the same full, unfiltered entry list RF07 already renders, without navigating away from or restarting "Meus Registros".
108	- **FR-009**: When an active search and/or filter combination matches zero entries on an account that has entries, the screen MUST show a distinct "no results" state separate from RF07's account-wide zero-entries empty state, with a way to adjust or clear the applied criteria.
109	- **FR-010**: Whenever a search or filtered fetch fails outright — whether because the device is offline, the request times out, or the response is malformed — the screen MUST continue showing whatever search/filter results are already present in the local cache rather than discarding them, and MUST present a clear, retryable error. Specifically for the offline case, upon reconnection the system MUST reconcile the displayed results with what the server currently returns for the same criteria without duplicating any entry.
110	- **FR-011**: This unit MUST NOT implement entry tag or category creation, editing, or filtering (extension feature, requirements section 2), export (RF05), chat (RF04), or any other later-unit behavior; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.
111	
112	### Key Entities
113	
114	- **Search Query**: The free-text term the user has typed into the search bar, debounced before being sent as the `q` parameter to `GET /entries/search`; empty when the user has typed nothing or has cleared it.
115	- **Filter Set**: The combination of date-range choice and selected entry types the user has applied via the filter sheet, sent as `dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`source` parameters. The date range and the entry-type selection are combined with AND logic with each other and with any active Search Query; when more than one entry type is selected, the resulting requests (one per type) are combined with OR logic among themselves, since `source` is single-valued and each entry has exactly one type.
116	- **Active Filter Chip**: A removable, on-screen representation of one currently applied Filter Set criterion, shown under the search bar whenever that criterion is active.
117	- **Search Result Entry**: A Journal Entry (as already defined by RF07) as returned by `GET /entries/search` or `GET /entries` under the current Search Query and Filter Set, ordered by relevance to an active query rather than strictly by recency when a query is present. When more than one entry type is selected, this is the merged, de-duplicated (by entry ID) combination of each per-type request's results, re-sorted into that same ordering.
118	
119	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
120	
121	### Measurable Outcomes
122	
123	- **SC-001**: For each of the three documented seed-data search terms, searching finds its matching entry even though the entry's text never contains that literal word, 100% of the time.
124	- **SC-002**: A burst of fast typing produces exactly one search request per pause in typing, never one request per keystroke, across all tested typing sequences.
125	- **SC-003**: Applying filter criteria across different axes (date range, entry type, search term) together always narrows results to entries matching every active axis at once (AND), with zero observed cases of an axis being ignored; applying two or more entry-type chips together always returns the union of entries matching any of them (OR within that one axis), with zero observed cases of an entry type's matches being excluded because another type was also selected.
126	- **SC-004**: 100% of currently applied filters are visible on screen as a chip, with the funnel button shown in its active state whenever at least one filter is applied.
127	- **SC-005**: Clearing filters, whether by removing every chip individually or by using "Limpar filtros", always restores the full, unfiltered list without the user leaving or reloading the screen.
128	- **SC-006**: After a period offline followed by reconnection, a search/filter result list never shows a duplicated entry and matches what the server currently returns for the same criteria.
129	
130	## Assumptions
131	
132	- This unit makes live the search bar and funnel button that RF07 already renders as visual-fidelity placeholders on "Meus Registros" (per RF07's own FR-008 and its Assumptions), rather than building new UI chrome for them.
133	- Combining an active search term with the filter sheet at the same time is governed by the same AND-logic rule the requirement states for multiple filters, even though the prototype does not show the two interacting explicitly (prototype extract, implementation note 7) — a reasonable extension of an explicitly stated rule, not an invented behavior.
134	- A distinct "no results for this search/filter" message is shown when an active search/filter combination narrows an otherwise non-empty account down to zero entries, kept separate from RF07's account-wide "Nenhum registro ainda" empty state, since the two represent different situations (a true empty account vs. an empty result of the user's own narrowing).
135	- Search and filter errors (timeout, malformed response, offline) are surfaced using the same retryable error-handling pattern already established for this screen's other network calls (RNF09), without inventing a new error presentation specific to search.
136	- Active search text and filters are not persisted beyond the current viewing of "Meus Registros" — leaving and later returning to the screen starts from its default, unfiltered state — since neither the requirements nor the prototype describe any persistence for them.
137	- The "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" per-entry badge, tag chips, and date-group headings on each result card behave exactly as RF07 already defined; this unit changes which entries are shown and in what order, not how an individual result card renders.
